reason: I'll strengthen the bone framework first; the picture shows spaces for mineral and says it resists compression.
expectation: I expect the mineral to fill the framework and make the bones stronger.

alternatives.reason: Building the front muscle also fits a goal, but I'll prepare the bones first.
The back muscle is another goal, but I don't see a reason to build it before the bones.

effect: The mineral strengthened the bones while leaving the elbow joint movable. Now I need to build and attach both muscles.
reaction: The contrast between hard bone and the still-movable joint makes sense.
reason: I'll build the front muscle first; the connective tissue should help assemble the muscle cells.
expectation: I expect a front muscle made from the cells and supporting tissue, though I'm not sure exactly how the tissue fits.

alternatives.reason: The back muscle is also needed, but I have no clear reason to build it first.

effect: The front muscle is the biceps; its cells join into fibres, and the supporting tissue continues into tendon ends.
reaction: The time strip and tendon connection make the assembly clearer.
reason: I'll build the back muscle too, so both muscles are ready to attach on opposite sides.
expectation: I expect the back cells and connective tissue to form a back upper-arm muscle with tendon ends.

alternatives.reason: I could attach the biceps now, but I want to build the other muscle first.

effect: Both muscles are built; the triceps sits at the back and has tendon ends that attach across the elbow.
reaction: Its similar construction to the biceps makes the two muscles easy to compare.
reason: I'll attach the biceps first to start placing the muscles on opposite sides of the elbow.
expectation: I expect the biceps to attach to the skeleton at the front of the elbow.

alternatives.reason: The triceps also needs attaching, but I don't see a reason it must go first.

effect: The biceps is attached across the front of the elbow, where its pull bends the forearm. The triceps still needs to go on the back.
reaction: The arrows make the biceps' pull and the resulting bend clear.
reason: I'll attach the triceps to complete the pair; it's the only offered combination.
expectation: I expect the triceps to attach behind the elbow so its pull can help straighten the arm.

effect: The finished arm shows how muscles on opposite sides pull to bend and straighten the elbow.
reaction: The two views make the opposing pulls clear and satisfying.

mostWorthwhile.text: Attaching the triceps was most worthwhile: seeing both muscles shorten and lengthen made the two directions of movement understandable.

leastWorthwhile.text: Building the triceps felt a little repetitive after the similar biceps assembly, though comparing them was useful.

surprise.text: The supporting tissue continues into tendon ends, connecting the muscle assembly to its attachments.

arbitrary.text: No action felt purposeless, though I had no clear reason to choose the front muscle before the back one.

continue.text: I would continue: building the arm made the connection between its parts and movement clear, and I'd be curious to see another body system assembled.
